claims.claim: Core Scientific's June 30, 2026 10-Q quantifies counterparty concentration: CoreWeave represented about 77% of six-month total revenue and all HPC colocation revenue was derived from that single customer.

Leverage is a material resilience constraint: the filing reports about $4.4B of aggregate principal indebtedness at June 30, 2026, including a $3.3B 7.75% senior secured notes financing used to refinance the term loan and fund development-related obligations.

Physical capacity conversion is an execution falsifier: 395 MW was billable against 590 MW leased at June 30, leaving 195 MW in construction/commissioning; contracted demand therefore should not be treated as equivalent to operating revenue capacity.

risks: confidence inflation from equating leased MW with billable MW
competition for diversified high-density colocation customers

contradictions.contradiction: Large contracted/leased HPC capacity supports demand visibility, while current revenue concentration and leverage make cash-flow resilience unusually dependent on counterparty performance and timely capacity delivery.

unknowns: economics and credit profile of future non-CoreWeave customers
timing/cost to convert remaining leased MW into billable capacity
falsifiers: Meaningful revenue diversification across multiple high-quality HPC customers would reduce counterparty concentration risk.
On-time conversion of leased MW to billable capacity with durable debt-service coverage would weaken execution/leverage concerns.

assist.changedStrategy: Used the current 10-Q to quantify counterparty concentration, leverage and leased-versus-billable capacity rather than repeating generic HPC-demand risk.
